=== THE CENTRAL CLAIM WAS NOT TAKEN ON TRUST -- I REPRODUCED IT FROM SCRATCH ===
This PR's deliverable is an OBSERVATION (build-plan 1.8: the hook fires from hooks.json in a real live session). An observation claim is worth exactly as much as its reproducibility, so I re-ran it independently in this session's own container, which happens to carry the same claude CLI 2.1.282 / Python 3.11.15 / Ubuntu 24.04.4 the doc names.

(1) Bash matcher, reproduced. Ran the doc's section-1 command verbatim (own scratch dir, own LWB_LEDGER_PATH, --plugin-dir at plugins/claude/lwb, --settings allow [Bash, Task], --permission-mode dontAsk, --output-format json). Exit 0; result 'It printed exactly: `hello-lwb-hook-test`'; ledger gained EXACTLY ONE line: {"hook_event": "PreToolUse", "tool_name": "Bash", "permit": true, "warnings": ["lwb 0.1.0: reporting only, no policy enforced yet"], "findings": [{"rule_id": "lwb_version", "mode": "warn", ...}]} -- shape-identical to the doc's recorded line.

(2) Agent matcher, reproduced. Ran the doc's section-2 command verbatim. Exit 0; result 'The subagent returned exactly: `subagent-lwb-hook-test-ok`'; transcript subagent_stats {"spawned": 1, "completed": 1, "by_type": {"general-purpose": 1}}; ledger gained EXACTLY ONE line with tool_name "Agent". This independently confirms the doc's empirical note that PreToolUse reports a Task-tool dispatch under the matcher name "Agent".

(3) NEGATIVE CONTROL -- the evidence is NOT vacuous. The single most important thing a reviewer can do to an observation claim is check that the observed signal is actually caused by the mechanism claimed. I copied plugins/claude/lwb to a scratch dir, DELETED hooks/hooks.json from the copy, and re-ran the identical section-1 prompt against that copy. The session still ran and still made a real Bash dispatch ('It printed exactly: `hello-lwb-hook-test`'), and NO ledger file was created at all. So the ledger line is produced specifically because hooks.json registers the hook -- not by plugin presence, not by session startup. The claim 'fires FROM hooks.json' is established, not merely correlated.
